summary: This note is a summary infobox for the list of US Open women's singles champions, covering the tournament's history from its 1887 creation through 2017. It reports the tournament's location, governing body, surface changes by era, prize money for 2016, and the record holders for most titles and consecutive titles. It also names the 2017 champion, Sloane Stephens.
one_line: Infobox-style overview of US Open women's singles history, record title holders, surfaces, prize money and the 2017 champion.
key_facts: The US Open was created in 1887 and had 130 editions as of 2017.
The US Open women's singles has been held at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Queens, New York City, United States.
The tournament's governing body is the USTA.
The US Open was played on grass from 1887 to 1974, on clay from 1975 to 1977, and on hard courts from 1978 to the present.
Total prize money for the 2016 US Open was US $36,324,000.
The winner's prize money at the 2016 US Open was US $3,500,000.
Molla Bjurstedt Mallory holds the amateur-era record for most women's singles titles with 8.
Chris Evert and Serena Williams each hold the open-era record for most women's singles titles with 6.
Molla Bjurstedt Mallory and Helen Jacobs each won 4 consecutive titles in the amateur era.
Chris Evert holds the open-era record for most consecutive titles with 4.
Sloane Stephens is the current champion, having won the 2017 women's singles title.
The note lists 50 editions in the Open Era as of 2017.
